  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo

(6) PUBLIC HEARING:

6A. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2019-001 (ZCA-2019-001) TO CHAPTER
12 C-S ZONE. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment
2019-001 (ZCA-2019-001) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal
Code to allow towing service with ancillary vehicle storage and
ancillary vehicle inspection in the C-S (Commercial Service) zone
citywide.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs Larry asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019

  Within the conditions, would there be any restrictions to the
  size or height of the vehicles? Also, there was no mention of
  boats, are there any or are they restricted or exempt? Also,
  are boats considered to be vehicles and would they be restricted
  also?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that boats would be within the category of
  trailers, due to being transported on trailers and trailers
  are not acceptable.
  Zoning Code Amendments in the C3 zone – What about storing of
  vehicles or towing services with ancillary storage?
  - Ms. Fewell stated no – towing service is not allowed in any
  of the zones within the city currently. Staff has historically
  categorized towing services as vehicle storage, and that
  designation is only allowed in the manufacturing zones.
  So this Zoning Code Amendment will help to clear or give these
  services a classification?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 Would the Zoning Code Amendment open up additional locations
  for vehicle storage/towing?
  - Ms. Fewell stated it would allow the use of the CS Zone
  through special use permit approval.
 So currently, it is not allowed in the CS?
  - Ms. Fewell stated correct.
 So if this request is approved, the city would now allow more
  towing services in Inglewood, which would increase the sixteen
  already established towing services we have at present, correct?
  - Ms. Fewell stated correct.
 At present, vehicle storage which is allowed in the M-1 and M-
  2 zones is the only location where vehicle storage which
  basically means towing is allowed, correct?
  - Ms. Fewell stated correct.
 Why is this coming before the Planning Commission now to open
  up this CS zoned property for vehicle towing/storage services,
  which is already a very busy, heavily traveled corridor – was
  it because the applicant realized that the location where he
  wanted to conduct his business was not zoned for that use, and
  the only way he could have his business in that area would
  require the zone to be re-designated for the entire city to now
  allow vehicle towing/storage services?
  - Ms. Fewell stated correct.
 She asked staff to point-out on the map, all of the CS zones in
  the City, where on the map the location of the new business and
  what areas would the zoned area change effect the city with the
  new designation.
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the various areas of the city that
  would be effected would include La Brea Boulevard starting at
  Spruce Avenue and heading south on La Brea/Hawthorne
  Boulevard to 104th Street or the city boundary.
 Then she stated with the approval of this zone change it would
  open the main corridor of the city to be over-run with even more
  auto-related businesses and services, also allowing very
  unpleasing landscapes of six-foot high fencing not very
  esthetically pleasing to the eye and take away from the enhanced
  spatial experience which is where this city is going toward
  improving everything that we possibly can. Several of our
  neighboring communities have enhanced their landscaping, also
  cleaning up a lot of businesses and their main street
  thoroughfares such as Lennox, Hawthorne, Lawndale and Torrance.

  2
   Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
  September 4, 2019

    She also stated that the City of Inglewood has sixteen like
  businesses already within a nine square-foot mile City. The
  appropriate location for these types of businesses would be in
  the M-1 & M-2 zones.

  Chairman Springs asked Commissioner Trejo if she would possibly
  save any further questions for the applicant, and she stated that
  she would do so.

  Commissioner Coleman asked –
   Say an applicant receives an approval for a towing yard on the
  CS corridor and then six months later applies for another
  approval for a like business, and applies for another – does
  the applicant have to return to the city and come before the
  planning commission to request approval again and again each
  time or does the applicant have a cart blanche’ authorization
  and only has to apply once? How does it work?
  - Ms. Fewell stated the city is recommending first the special
  use permit approval, so each new towing business that comes
  into the CS zone, must obtain an approval through an SUP.
  Then there is a business requirement of 1,000 foot separation
  between an active towing business and then the new request
  coming in. In general, the 1,000 feet separation would equal
  typically two mega(super) blocks.

  Commissioner Rice asked staff:
   Would the separation between businesses apply to both sides of
  the street, if there was an approved towing business in the CS
  zone would that apply to the opposite side of the street or is
  it just linear distance? Is the map being used this evening for
  demonstrative purposes only, whereas the CS zone actually goes
  further, starting at Florence Boulevard all the way south to
  104th Street – actually the city’s border to border?
  - Ms. Fewell stated – it would be on both sides – property to
  property. This map is pulled from the City’s GIS Dept., this
  is the actual live map, and the distance covers from Spruce
  to 104th Street.

  Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward and address
  the planning commission.

  Mr. Robert Rudolph, representative for the applicant, and Mr.
  Robert Van Langen, Employee; addressed the planning commission.

  Chairman Springs opened the floor for questions to the applicants
  by the planning commission.

  Commissioner Holly asked –
   Just two questions – the first, where is your subject site
  located presently (asking staff to show the GIS map for visual)?
  - Mr. Rudolph stated they were located just one block south of
  Century Boulevard, on 102nd Street and Hawthorne Boulevard,
  on the west side of the street.
   In the staff report, it states “with ancillary vehicle
  inspections”, for clarification explain what does “with
  ancillary vehicle inspections” entail?
-  Mr. Rudolph stated that it could be for impound or a police request
  most of the time, generally all the time. And that car is held u

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019

Commissioner Rice stated:
 His question is for staff first, will this project site be up
  for design review? Will staff require a six-foot enclosed
  landscaped wall for compliance?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated no regarding Design Review at the planning
  commission level, but yes at the staff level for this project.
  - Mr. Rudolph stated that they will be working with staff to
  insure that they comply with all landscaping requirements and
  directions for beautification of our wall, and they will
  comply with the enclosed six-foot wall.

Commissioner Trejo stated:
 That this request is not for just one tow service application
  or business, but for opening the entire corridor for multiple
  tow services - if this action is approved.
 Then she asked Mr. Rudolph about the fact that they have been
  at this present location which is a CS Zone location for over
  1-yr., when they attempted to acquire their business license
  and found out that this location could not be used for this type
  of business, what happened next?
  - Mr. Rudolph stated that they were in the process of having a
  contractor assist them with some remodeling and there was
  some misunderstanding all around, so when they attempted to
  secure the garage with some better doors and in attempting to
  make the garage facility area stronger, that’s when we learned
  at that time through the field inspector that there was an
  issue with us being at this site.
 She stated that with this information the applicant went to
  obtain a business license, but could not without having to
  change the entire CS Zone corridor to allow for this type of
  location, but multiple areas and sites in the City.
 She then asked Mr. Reynolds how many vehicles can be stored on
  a 30,000+ square foot property.
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that it is over 30,000 square feet, and
  the storage capacity is about 80 to 100 cars, he would have
  to consult with his staff for the actual numbers, if he could
  do that right now… And, how many tow trucks at the site?
  - Mr. Robert Van Langen of B&H Tow, stated that if all the
  vehicles are packed in tightly, there is the potential of 200
  cars, but that is regulation, and at present we have 77
  vehicles on the lot, generally we run between 60 to 79 cars
  with 12 Tow Trucks on site.
 She also stated that with using the range of 60-79 cars and the
  12 trucks, the applicant’s lot will have a possible 90 vehicles
  on site. She then asked staff what are the requirements for tow
  service allotment of vehicles and parking lot requirements for
  improvement’s and maintenance on a site? Would it be specific
  to this applicant’s tow service or is there a general blanket
  requirement to obtain a Special Use Permit for this CS zone?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that yes this applicant would be subject to
  the City’s parking lot improvement requirements essentially
  require a 3.5 foot half wall and a landscaping buffer around
  parking lots with lighting and amenities along those lines,
  to be included. The way the CS zone code amendment has been
  drafted would require a 6-foot high screen wall around the
  storage areas of the site, but not the general parking areas.
  In those general areas, the parking lot improvements of the
  3.5 foot wall would be in effect. Also note that the code as
  currently written, allows for a commercial property to build
  a 6-foot high wall along their property line with a landscaped
  buffer, and this proposed code amendment is written to require
  a six-foot high screening wall around the storage areas.
  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019

Commissioner Coleman asked:
 If a constituent has been towed after a long evening of enjoying
  the city’s events with Hollywood Park and maybe at the Forum,
  etc., and finds that their vehicle has been towed to this site,
  will there be staff available 24 hours who can assist with the
  retrieving of that constituent’s vehicle? Per the staff report,
  you state that you will have the office opened only from 7:00am
  until 10:00pm.
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that there will be a staff person at the
  office to inform the tow truck driver on duty that there is
  an customer at the office attempting to do a pick-up of their
  vehicle that has been deposited in the tow yard, then staff
  would inform the customer that the tow truck driver is out at
  a location, and once he has completed his task, he will return
  to the yard to assist with the release of the individual’s
  vehicle.
 Then he stated that it is not fair to the constituent who is
  there say after 1:00am or 2:00am in the morning attempting to
  retrieve their vehicle to have to sit or stand outside of a tow
  yard and wait for a tow truck driver who is on the other side
  of the city or in another city’s location, dealing with the
  events there, and will most likely be at that location for about
  an hour or two, all the while the constituent has to wait, when
  there should be several staff members at the tow yard already
  who can assist that individual, so that they will not have to
  stay out until 3:00am waiting for their vehicle to be released.
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that if there is a staff member at the
  tow yard after 10:00pm, he will not be the one to retrieve
  the vehicle, that is what the tow truck driver does, and if
  there is no staff member in the office, there will be a 24
  hour dispatch number posted, like a dispatch who will contact
  the tow truck driver and notify him that there is an
  individual at the yard who is there to pick-up his vehicle.
  - Mr. Van Langen stated that there will always be a staff member
  in the office at all times, definitely it will be open for a
  full 24 hours, and the individual will see staff at the site,
  and staff will contact the tow truck driver, so there will
  not be a long wait.

Chairman Springs asked –
 How long has your tow service been in business and here in the
  City Inglewood?
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that they have been in the towing business
  since 1957.
 He then asked how many locations here in the City of Inglewood
  and where exactly are they located?
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that their previous location was 1149
  South La Brea, and then moved to La Brea and Florence Blvd.,
  - Mr. Ikemefuna stated that there was one on La Brea, just north
  of Century Blvd.
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that they only have one location, the
  present one.
 He asked the applicant if this location becomes too small where
  you feel that you will need a second location to hold more cars,
  will you purchase another?
  - Mr. Reynolds stated that the property costs here in Inglewood
  have become so expensive, they feel unable to afford another
  property. He stated that in the City of Torrance, they do
  have another property that is six acres, and will be able to
  hold any overflow that may arise, such as big vehicles and or
  trailers and the like.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019
  If you would explain what would be the benefit to the community
  of your place of business being located in this CS Zone, what
  would help to make the lives of the members of this community
  better that would make this planning commission approve your
  request tonight?
  - There is a benefit to the police department to have a facility
  within the City of Inglewood, having the storage of the
  vehicles local to assist with the police department’s
  investigations and CSI procedures not having to travel
  outside of the city limits to other nearby cities. It’s more
  convenient for the residents of the City of Inglewood so that
  when they are attempting to locate and retrieve their
  vehicles, they do not have to travel far to other outlying
  cities to find their vehicles, they’re here within their own
  city.
  Now you stated that you do have another large lot in Torrance,
  is that correct?
  - Yes, that is for the overflow of vehicles when this local lot
  is full.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 Based on the scale presented tonight, it looks like the maximum
  of storage facilities or towing companies that would be using
  the ancillary parking in the CS Zone, using the thousand foot
  spacing radius before would not be very many, possibly only
  four.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated yes.
  - Ms. Fewell stated with utilizing the thousand foot spacing
  radius between each of the businesses, it would most likely
  only be four max.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments to speak
for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST

None

Chairman Springs called for questions and final remarks from the
planning commission.

Commissioner Holly stated –
 Through the CS Zone area, it’s predominately automotive sales
  and vehicle repair shops, I know where the applicant is located
  and some small shops. There’s not a lot of space for more tow
  yards to come into the area. Their location is near the end of
  the city limits and so Commissioner Holly does not feel this is
  a problem and is in favor.

Chairman Springs asked Commissioner Holly a question –
 Will it give an appealing presence in the area or will it look
  like a large big white walled building, all enclosed with no
  landscaping (and he states he probably should have asked the
  applicant)…

Commissioner Holly responded –
 It would depend on the design review with City Staff. What staff
  is saying that the structure can be made to be more appealing
  to the eye, but if you look at it today, it gives the appearance
  of a car dealership, and mainly that is what is in the area
  surrounding the applicant, reiterating that there are only small
  businesses and car dealerships in that area.

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019

Chairman Springs asked –
 So, the applicant’s main business is to pick-up vehicles that
  were in an accident or being towed for “City Purposes”, so if
  the applicant were to pick-up a vehicle that has been in a major
  accident...

Commissioner Holly replied –
 For “City Purposes”, if you were near, you would never see it,
  as the vehicle would be kept behind a fence.

Commissioner Rice asked –
 For clarification of the code, a commercial business must have
  a three-foot fence around the property, landscaping, decorative
  design in front of the property, including public parking to
  allow people to enter the premises and retrieve their impounded
  vehicles and I believe there is a wall behind there will be a
  six-feet, the decor will come into play with the little off-
  site parking they would have and any other commercial property.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated she would like to clarify regarding the
  requirements of the six-foot high wall – that wall can be
  placed relatively close to the property line and our code
  presently allows this. It also allows a six-foot high wall on
  the property line or anywhere 20 feet into the property. There
  are also design guidelines that require a landscaped buffer,
  along the property line as well.

Commissioner Trejo stated –
 She stated the fact that the planning commission is not going
  through a Special Use Permit process in order to allow this
  applicant to receive approval for his application, the planning
  commission is not going through this process right now, but what
  the planning commission is doing right now is voting on a zone
  change that would affect not only the site where the applicant
  is, but the entire area of the city and that is her concern.
  The reason this zone change is being voted on is because
  unfortunately when the applicant opened his establishment a full
  year ago, for whatever the reason this occurred, the applicant
  was not made aware that he could not open this type of business
  in this zone and would have to be opened in another zone, the
  applicant picked a site that does not allow it and now the
  applicant has returned seeking approval of his site location
  and planning commission is going to have to allow not only the
  applicant’s request because we don’t just offer a special
  privilege to one individual, but we will have to change the
  entire zoned area to allow this type of business for everyone
  who applies and affect several areas of the City, and that is
  her concern. She stated that she is aware of the area, she knows
  what businesses are there, but the fact that they are not being
  asked to decide about the applicant opening a tow truck service
  at the site, but that this body is being asked to do a zone
  change which will affect several zones.

Chairman Springs asked Commissioner Trejo –
 So the question is once the area has been approved for change,
  then anyone else can come to the City to apply to open a tow
  truck service in that area?

Commissioner Trejo replied –
 The applicants would have to come to the City to apply for a
  Special Use Permit, but yes.
  - Ms. Fewell stated that anyone applying to open in this
  particular area must be approved through the Special Use
  Permit process and would not be permitted by right.
  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 4, 2019

Chairman Springs asked Ms. Fewell –
 With the changing of the zone to allow towing services, will it
  be necessary for a Special Use Permit to be opened for another
  like business in that zone, once the zone has been changed?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that this zone change is for the zone text
  amendment which is to allow this type of business use in this
  zone.

Commissioner Trejo stated –
 Once the zone is changed, and if applicants want to open a
  towing service and since the zone allows the use, then the
  applicant can file for a special use permit, so the applicant
  would still have to come in.
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, the applicant would have to meet all
  of the site development standards, with the minimal square
  footage, and linear footage, and after meeting those
  requirements, they would still have to come before the
  Planning Commission for the Special Use Permit approval.

Commissioner Coleman stated –
 In case all are not aware, that any towing service is not
  restricted to just the area they are stationed in, like here in
  Inglewood, they can conduct business in other local and
  surrounding areas they choose to work in, which could result in
  overflow of vehicles, unkempt sites, that can look terrible.
  Along the area on Hawthorne Boulevard, there are no new car sale
  lots, bright and shiny vehicles, but an overconcentration of
  used car sale lots only, with low-end, repossessed vehicles that
  are not too pleasing to look at and with both type businesses
  attempting to open here in Inglewood with their overflowing
  vehicles, He said that this is a concern of his.
 He also said, with the approval of the zone change will be like
  opening the flood-gates where the City could possibly be
  inundated with like businesses and their unkempt practices of
  conducting business, because they see what potential of money
  making there can be here in the City, especially with all of
  the influx of commercial building and activities.

Chairman Springs closed and thanked the Planning Commission for
all of their input, and asked for a motion regarding the zone
change.

The motion was made by Commissioner Holly to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2019-091 and adopt a resolution recommending

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND
  RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT ZCA-2O19-001 TO AMEND
  CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE
  (IMC) TO ALLOW TOWING SERVICE IN THE C-S
  (COMMERCIAL SERVICE) ZONE CITYWIDE

Be approved.

  motion, which is to add a requirement to page three of the City
  Council Resolution, item(c), with this statement - of a 24 hour,
  staffed in-office service availability for customers to be able

  business hours of operation.

Chairman Springs stated –

  to be opened for 24 hours?

6B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-009 (SP-2019-009) AT 10901 CRENSHAW
BOULEVARD. A public hearing to consider an application by Othman
Ghalab, representing Family Market, for a Special Use Permit No.
2019-009 (SP-2019-009) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-
site consumption within an existing convenience market on an
approximately 20,970 square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned
property at 10901 Crenshaw Boulevard.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 If there was a crime report for that area in the planning
